title: Microprofile collection spec and regression observations
content:
Purpose:
This doc specifies the microprofile signals we should collect from the serving runtime, the lightweight collection and retention strategy for running continuous microbenchmarks and trace-driven captures, and an initial set of regression-detection heuristics and playbook steps. It is intended to be an operational spec for the bench infra and a short incident-reference for regressions detected by CI and production probes.

Scope:
- Kernel execution timings and selection metadata for each request
- KV-cache events: hit/miss, warmup latency, eviction cause, victim id hashes (anonymized)
- Batch composition metrics: batch size, occupancy ratio, batch formation delay
- Scheduler decisions: preempt, coalesce, queue delay, node affinity tag
- Minimal request-level tracing (span ids, sampled timelines) to link kernel/kv/batcher decisions to tail-latency spikes

Definitions (quick):
- microprofile: a short (~1s to 30s) sampling window capturing a compact set of high-signal metrics per request
- trace-sample: full span timeline for a single request, used for root-cause reproduction
- hotset: working set of KV keys that should be resident for a workload; used for warmup experiments

Design constraints and goals:
- Low overhead: per-request added CPU should be < 1% at production QPS; sampling should be rate-limited by default
- Useful fidelity: kernel timings must be accurate to +/- 25us at 95% CI for short kernels
- Privacy: key ids are hashed and truncated; no PII or customer prompt text is captured in these artifacts
- Deterministic replays: collected microprofiles and traces should be usable to seed the bench generator to reproduce the distribution of sequence lengths and hotset churn

Signal catalog (fields to collect per microprofile):
- profile_id: short unique id for the sample (uuid v4)
- ts: epoch ms captured at sample start
- model: model name & pinned version (e.g., redwood-3b-v2)
